mechanicTruth: Tread grooves grip by channeling water and snow out from under the contact patch, so as the grooves get shallow that channeling drops off: wet traction fades below about 3/32 inch and snow traction below about 4/32, both still above the 2/32 legal minimum.
selectedCaption: 2/32" is the legal minimum. It is not the safe one. Below 3/32", hydroplaning risk climbs sharply in rain. Below 4/32", you lose meaningful grip in snow. Legal and safe are two different numbers — and they matter at different times of year. Worth checking before the next storm, not after.
voiceoverScript: Legal tread is not safe tread. Shallow grooves move less water, so rain grip fades. Snow needs more open groove. Two depths, two seasons. One check answers both.

storyboardBeats.visual: Macro of a slim metal tread probe sinking into a wet tire groove, rain falling, dark wet asphalt catching distant streetlight reflections
storyboardBeats.motion: slow push-in as rain beads on the rubber
storyboardBeats.narration: Legal tread is not safe tread.

storyboardBeats.visual: A cut tire section on a bench with water poured across the tread, the deep grooves carrying it out and away while a thin film pools on the flat rubber
storyboardBeats.motion: slow tilt following the water out of the groove
storyboardBeats.narration: Shallow grooves move less water, so rain grip fades.

storyboardBeats.visual: The same cut tire section with its grooves packed solid with wet snow, almost no open channel left, cold blue side light
storyboardBeats.motion: slow push-in on the packed groove

storyboardBeats.visual: Two tire sections side by side on the bench, one with deep square-shouldered grooves, the other worn nearly smooth, soft studio key light
storyboardBeats.motion: slow lateral slide from the deep tread to the worn one

storyboardBeats.visual: The metal probe standing upright in a wet tire groove under streetlight again, rain returning and beading across the rubber
storyboardBeats.motion: slow pull-back mirroring the opening shot
